question.text: For G-Sec cash-settled Interest Rate Derivatives, client-level position limits are typically expressed in terms of which of the following?

answer.text: A percentage of open interest in the contract or an absolute rupee amount (whichever is higher), calibrated by maturity bucket
A fixed Rs. 500 crore client cap applied uniformly to every client across all contracts and maturities
A flat 3% of the outstanding stock of the underlying bond, with no open-interest reference
The client's average daily turnover over the past quarter, with no maturity-bucket differentiation

explanation.text: The Logic: Client-level position limits for G-Sec cash-settled IRD are built around open interest in the contract — typically expressed as a percentage of open interest or an absolute rupee amount, whichever is higher — and are calibrated separately for different maturity buckets. This ties allowed client exposure to actual contract liquidity rather than to a single static rupee cap or an outstanding-stock-only formula. To assess whether a particular client position is in violation, one needs the total open interest figure and the bucket-specific limit, not just the outstanding stock. The Trap: A uniform fixed Rs. 500 crore client cap across all contracts ignores both open interest and maturity bucket. A pure 3%-of-outstanding-stock formula leaves out the open-interest dimension entirely. Average daily turnover is an activity metric, not a position-limit basis. Compliance assessments require the actual open-interest and bucket figures. Note: The cited workbook (NISM Series IV, pages 234-237) describes client position limits for G-Sec cash-settled IRD in terms of open interest and maturity bucket (e.g., 3% of open interest or Rs. 400/Rs. 200 crore whichever is higher), and does not support the fixed "Rs. 500 crore client cap derived from outstanding stock" framing used in the original numeric version of this item. The framing above mirrors the structural description in the workbook without claiming a specific numeric breach from outstanding stock alone.
